notes: GPUI PANEL. The target UI framework is GPUI 0.2.2 (Zed's framework), not React, and you have no training knowledge of its exact API. Before writing, read: the finished panel crates as worked examples (rever-ui-traffic, rever-ui-history, rever-ui-menus: their src and examples/preview.rs show how views, listeners, hover, scrolling, text fields, theme, strings and previews are done here), every file in rever-ui-kit/src, and vendor/gpui/src/elements/*.rs plus vendor/gpui/examples/*.rs for exact method names. Build a view struct implementing gpui::Render that reproduces the React component's layout, sizes, colors and behaviors: the cookies / local storage / session storage tabs, the table with sorting and filtering, inline editing, add, delete, clear, import and export, and any detail view. The component makes many IPC calls (`window.rev.*`) to read and change cookies and storage: define one trait in this crate with a method per operation (async or returning a result through a callback, your choice, but usable from a GPUI view), which the host implements later; the preview uses an in-memory fake that really applies the edits so the behaviors can be exercised. Colors and sizes come from src/renderer/src/styles.css (tokens in rever_ui_kit::theme::Theme; define a missing one locally and list it). User-facing strings go through `rever_ui_kit::i18n::Lang::t(key)` with the keys the TSX uses. Keep logic (sorting, filtering, parsing imports, validation) in plain functions with Korean-named unit tests; the file gets the `Port of` marker only when its behaviors are all there. Preview: fill examples/preview.rs so `cargo run -p rever-ui-storage --example preview_storage` shows the panel with fixture data; capture with `scripts/capture-window.sh preview_storage /tmp/preview_storage.png`, read the PNG, compare with the TSX, fix what is off. Do not bring windows to the front, do not capture the screen any other way, do not run the `rever` app, and never run cargo without `-p` (other crates in the workspace are mid-edit).
